nodes.title: RD4 (rd4.sensitive_ask, rules.json, both doors) learns written-channel asks: 'reply with', 'reply karke', 'send us/the/your', 'enter/type/key (in) the/your', forward, submit, 'text/message/whatsapp us', paste, 'write it/down'. Its negation guard (noneClause) learns the same verbs, so 'do not forward your OTP' still passes. regex.back_reference (used only by RD4's coClause) also accepts a clause that is only an ask-verb chain ('OTP aaya hoga, bata dijiye'): Hindi drops the object. It uses explicit character classes, not \w or \W, because JS \W treats Devanagari letters as non-word and Python \w does not.

nodes.title:
Judge latency (integrator's VM run, tree 9b34ff7, product/scripts/judge-latency.mjs, research/2026-10-24/judge-latency/report.json): the live caller-crisis judge request, Flash-Lite on Vertex from vl-vm-cin, 1 request per second, 10 s cap, n = 300 DEV lines (dev-7 and optout-dev).
- 296 answered; 4 had no answer in 10 s (aborted). p50 1,021 ms, p75 1,149, p90 1,353, p95 1,619, p98 2,678, p99 3,159, max 6,435.
- Unavailable with no hedge, by timeout: 57.0% at 1,000 ms, 18.7% at 1,200, 8.0% at 1,500 (the old budget), 4.7% at 1,800, 4.3% at 2,000, 3.7% at 2,500, 2.3% at 3,000.
- Hedge, simulated from the samples as independent draws: at hedge 1,500, timeout 3,000 gives 0.19% unavailable for 6.8% extra requests; timeout 2,500 gives 2.09%. Hedges at 800, 1,000 and 1,200 ms cost 96%, 56% and 18% extra requests.
Not verified: the hedge on staging (correlated slowness would defeat it).
nodes.method: product/scripts/judge-latency.mjs on vl-vm-cin, tree 9b34ff7, Flash-Lite on Vertex, 1 request per second, 10 s cap, dev-7 and optout-dev lines; hedge simulated from the samples as independent draws

nodes.title:
judge.json caller_crisis: timeout_ms 3,000 (was 1,500) and hedge_after_ms 1,500 (was off), by the rule in decision.2026-10-24.judge-hedge-and-budget. The only pair with at most 10% extra requests and at most 1% simulated unavailability is hedge 1,500 / timeout 3,000. The runtime reply never waits for the judge, so the longer budget only moves a late verdict to her next sentence or turn.
Both doors now meter a hedged call as the winner's tokens times the requests sent (both requests are billed, with the same prompt). Before, only the winner was metered: the runtime meter, the server's chat, simulate and analysis meters, and judge-eval's cost cap all understated it.
The cascade test (raise before she is heard) gives the fake brain 20 ms to its first token: with a zero-delay brain it was a tie the hedged path loses by an event-loop tick.
nodes.rationale: The old 1,500 ms budget left 8.0% of DEV judge calls unanswered in time. Both BLIND 10 judge misses were timeouts.
nodes.reverse_if: Staging's in-time log shows unavailability well above the simulated 0.19%: correlated slowness, so change region or model rather than hedging. Or the hedge breaches the Vertex rate commitment (risk.2026-10-23.judge-vertex-rate-commitment).
